paper.title_en: Metric Source Completions and Integrability in Celestial Gravity
paper.abstract_en: Opposite-helicity soft limits carry ordering information, whereas a metric generating functional has a symmetric mixed response. We compare these structures for Einstein tree amplitudes, retaining the full momentum-conservation distribution. Normalized transport of primary sources fixes the metric response, and a common Banerjee--Pasterski prescription fixes the two ordered scattering currents on compact regular hard packets. At the reference metric, both ordered scattering responses agree with the transport Hessian, so the two matching defects vanish separately. A four-hard-particle example displays the same nonzero recoil coefficient in both orders and in the transport Hessian; an overlapping-source packet resolves the lower-order spin-frame contact. Six-graviton factorization independently tests the recoil and undifferentiated coefficients of the ordering difference. At seven points, angular integration produces a nonzero relative current whose connector variation contains a conjugate bulk term. We derive this term and its cancellation under coherent transport; global cubic scattering matching still requires the physical Ward comparison on the remaining singular overlaps. Transporting the states, kernels and inverse chains together gives a finite Ward identity and coefficientwise reconstruction for that chosen family. Regular packets leave extensions supported solely on excluded hard--hard coincidences undetermined, and the vacuum functional, independent of the hard sources, remains free.
